title: DeepSeek’s cost-saving AI may lead to inaccuracy in model performance: research
source_used: TechNode (9 Oct 2026) and 36Kr English edition (9 Oct 2026), found through Google News RSS; the SCMP original returned HTTP 403
key_facts: Researchers from ByteDance's Seed team identified a mechanism behind inconsistent long-context retrieval in DeepSeek models.

Chunked KV-cache compression, which packs groups of consecutive tokens into fewer cache entries to cut memory and attention costs, makes retrieval accuracy depend on where information falls inside a compression window, with differences of up to 40 percentage points across positions.
The team calls the pattern 'phase sensitivity' and reproduced it in models trained from scratch; different attention components specialise in retrieving information from different positions.
The findings explain how strong average benchmark results can conceal recurring retrieval weaknesses.

36Kr gives figures for the DeepSeek-V4 series in a 128K-token retrieval test: a 40.2-point gap for V4-Flash-Base and 34.8 for V4-Pro-Base, shrinking after post-training and to 6.1 points for V4.1-Flash-0910.
quote_evidence: Researchers from ByteDance's Seed team have identified a mechanism behind inconsistent long-context retrieval in DeepSeek models.

why_it_matters_hint: A memory-saving technique used by DeepSeek can make its models find the same fact in a long text or miss it depending on position.
